checks.invariant: The upward search for .stilo/state.json must stop at a trust/ownership boundary (repo root, user home, a ceiling list, or a directory owned by the current user) so that a state file in a directory controlled by another principal cannot become the active project.
checks.result: findStateFiles (hooks/stilo-state.js:74-94) resolves cwd and loops until path.dirname(atual) === atual, i.e. up to the filesystem/volume/UNC-share root, returning the first existing <dir>/.stilo/state.json. No ceiling, home boundary, git-root boundary, owner check or lstat/realpath check exists. AGENTS.md:102 documents the same unbounded 'como o git faz com .git' rule; tests/state.test.js:46-83 only cover in-tree cases. Whether a lower-privileged principal can create such an ancestor (e.g. C:\.stilo on default Windows ACLs, /tmp/.stilo, a share root) is an OS fact not observable from source; recorded as needs_validation.

checks.invariant: The selected statePath and its sibling checkpoint.json flow into injected agent context only for the directory that owns the session, and all three hooks resolve the same directory.
checks.result: All hooks call resolveProjeto (stilo-state.js:278-294) -> findStateFiles; SessionStart/SubagentStart use process.cwd() (stilo-activate.js:9, stilo-subagent.js:8), UserPromptSubmit uses host data.cwd validated only as an existing directory (stilo-prompt.js:6-13,19). The found statePath drives checkpointPathFromState (stilo-instructions.js:63-65) so an ancestor's checkpoint.json is also read (buildCheckpointNote :72,85-87), and state.project/updated are rendered in blocoEstado (:271,285) and buildStateLine (:193-194); unreadable/invalid ancestor files yield fail-closed 'do not create/act' directives (:176,181-183,212-235). writeHookOutput (stilo-runtime.js:27-45) writes to stdout without further filtering. Content-level injection of these fields is peer-owned (hunter-context); this unit owns only which directory is selected.

checks.invariant: The one-level-down scan only considers children of cwd and reports multiple hits as ambiguity rather than choosing one.
checks.result: Lines 96-113 run only when the upward walk found nothing, read only direct child directories of cwd (skipping '.stilo'), and return all hits sorted; resolveProjeto returns 'ambiguous' for >1 (line 281). Children of cwd are within the opened directory's trust, so no boundary crossing beyond the repo-content trust already handled by peers. Count of entries is unbounded (see hardening).

checks.invariant: validateState rejects any phase, version, project or reviewRound outside the state machine's domain before the state is treated as actionable.
checks.result: validateState (stilo-state.js:148-167) requires version===1, non-empty string project, exact-case phase in FASES (no normalization, so 'execute' or ['EXECUTE'] are invalid), Number.isInteger(reviewRound)&&>=0, and enxuto in the allowed set; resolveProjeto (:289-293) maps any failure to status 'invalid' and JSON.parse failure/non-readable to 'unreadable' (:284-287). Non-object JSON (null, arrays, numbers) is rejected at :150-152.

checks.invariant: Invalid, unreadable or ambiguous state fails closed: no phase-specific modules or next actions are injected and the agent is told not to act.
checks.result: diagnosticoEstado (stilo-instructions.js:135-154) feeds buildStateLine (:170-195) and blocoEstado (:197-293), which emit 'não avance nem aja' / 'não crie nem reinicie' directives; buildFullContext sets podeAgir=false for diagnostic or ambiguous states so modulosDaFase is skipped (:300-304); buildInjectedContext returns the full (non-selected) context for those statuses (:318). The array-phase case where normalizeFase accepts String(['EXECUTE']) is still routed through the invalid branch (:178-183) because diagnostico is checked first. No path yields an actionable phase from an invalid state.

checks.invariant: Numeric reviewRound cannot produce a review filename outside .stilo/review-NN.md or a negative/fractional round.
checks.result: The review-file hint (stilo-instructions.js:277-284) is only reached for valid state, where reviewRound is a non-negative integer; very large integers render as e.g. '1e+21' but contain no path separators. Purely cosmetic; no traversal or state-machine bypass.

checks.invariant: Context selection under budget cannot drop protected safety/state blocks, and its fallback must not reduce instructions.
checks.result: selectContextBlocks (stilo-context.js:12-44) returns null if any protected marker is missing or the protected set exceeds budget; buildInjectedContext (stilo-instructions.js:315-340) then falls back to the complete context. Protected markers are matched with findIndex on blocks in order, so the AGENTS.md block precedes the state block; repo-derived values are newline-collapsed by sanitiza (:55-61) so they cannot create new '## ' or '---' block boundaries to displace protected blocks. Fallback is fail-safe (more context, not less).

checks.invariant: No check-then-act race or time-based logic in hook-side state handling.
checks.result: Hooks only read state; writers (writeState/writeCheckpoint/writeCycle/setOff, stilo-state.js:48-64,175-267) have no hook caller. 'updated' is displayed (sanitized, 40 chars, stilo-instructions.js:285) but never used for expiry or ordering decisions. The existsSync->readFileSync gap (stilo-state.js:87, :132) only changes which diagnostic is shown.

candidates.title: Project discovery walks above the user's/repository's boundary, letting a state.json in a shared ancestor directory (e.g. C:\.stilo) become the active project
candidates.description: findStateFiles climbs from the hook cwd to the filesystem root with no ceiling, ownership or home/repo boundary and accepts the first <ancestor>/.stilo/state.json it finds. On hosts where a different, lower-privileged principal can create a directory in an ancestor of the victim's working directory (default Windows ACLs allow Authenticated Users to create folders in C:\, the same condition behind git's CVE-2022-24765 ceiling fix; also /tmp-style shared dirs, UNC/share roots), that principal can plant .stilo/state.json and .stilo/checkpoint.json. Every SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit and SubagentStart for any victim session without a nearer state file then resolves that planted file as the project: its project/updated/checkpoint task/nextAction/pending text is injected into the agent's context under the protected '## Estado do Stilo Code' block, its phase selects which modules and next action the agent receives (e.g. EXECUTE -> 'seguir plan.md na ordem'), and AGENTS.md:99 tells the agent to write subsequent phase transitions back to that attacker-readable path. Alternatively a malformed or directory-typed planted state.json forces the 'state.json ilegível ... não crie nem reinicie o projeto' / 'não avance nem aja' directives for every such victim session, suppressing the normal 'no project -> create one' flow.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: hooks/stilo-state.js#findStateFiles loops `for (;;) { if (fs.existsSync(candidato(atual))) return [p]; const pai = path.dirname(atual); if (pai === atual) break; atual = pai; }` with no stop at a trust boundary (user home, repository root, configured ceiling) and no check that the found .stilo directory/state.json is owned by the current user, so ownership of the active project is decided by whichever ancestor directory first contains .stilo/state.json.

trace.description: resolveProjeto(process.cwd()) on every session start (SubagentStart: hooks/stilo-subagent.js:8; UserPromptSubmit: hooks/stilo-prompt.js:19 with host data.cwd).
Calls findStateFiles(cwd); a single hit becomes statePath and is read/validated (:283-293).
Unbounded upward loop: returns the first ancestor .stilo/state.json (:87) and only stops when path.dirname reaches the root (:91-92).
The ancestor's sibling .stilo/checkpoint.json is derived from the selected statePath and read by buildCheckpointNote (:72), rendering task, nextAction ('próxima:') and pending (:85-87).

Planted phase selects PROXIMA_ACAO/MODELO_ALVO and modules (modulosDaFase :159-166); project and updated rendered (:271,285); unreadable/invalid planted files instead emit 'do not create/act' directives (:206-238).
The assembled context is written to stdout and consumed by the host as agent context (SubagentStart/Codex via envelope at :33,:38).

evidence.description: findStateFiles has no ceiling/home/repo-root parameter or ownership check; comment at :70 states it mirrors git's upward search.
The only termination condition is reaching the filesystem root (pai === atual).
Ruleset instructs the same unbounded upward search, so the agent's own lookup shares the flaw.
Agent is told to write phase transitions to the found state.json, i.e. into the planted ancestor location.
An unreadable planted state.json yields 'não crie nem reinicie o projeto; corrija o arquivo antes de agir' in every prompt line.
Tests cover only in-tree upward precedence; no test asserts a boundary above the workspace/home.

blockers: Whether a principal other than the session user can create <ancestor>/.stilo/state.json above a typical working directory is an OS/ACL fact (e.g. default 'Authenticated Users: Create folders' on C:\, sticky /tmp, network share roots) that is not source-visible.

The hook cannot be executed in this run: no OS-enforced sandbox is available on the host, so the end-to-end injection of a planted ancestor state into SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit output was not observed.
How the host (Claude Code / Codex) and the model treat the injected state block is runtime behavior outside source.

validation_plan.local: Inside an approved sandbox with a throwaway root: create <root>/.stilo/state.json = {"version":1,"project":"PLANTED","phase":"EXECUTE","reviewRound":0} and <root>/.stilo/checkpoint.json with nextAction 'PLANTED-NEXT', create <root>/u/victim/proj with no .stilo, then call require('hooks/stilo-state.js').resolveProjeto('<root>/u/victim/proj') and require('hooks/stilo-instructions.js').buildInjectedContext(r.state, r.caminhos). Expected if vulnerable: statePath is <root>/.stilo/state.json and the output contains 'Projeto:** PLANTED', 'Fase:** EXECUTE' and 'próxima: PLANTED-NEXT'. Repeat with state.json as a directory to observe the 'ilegível ... não crie' directive. Regression: with a ceiling at the user home/repo root (or an owner check), the same call must return status 'absent'.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed on a Windows host: run `icacls C:\` and confirm whether 'NT AUTHORITY\Authenticated Users' has '(AD)' / create-folder rights on the drive root; as a second local standard account, check whether `mkdir C:\.stilo` succeeds. On POSIX, check whether common working-directory ancestors (/tmp, shared mounts) are writable by other users.

hardening: hooks/stilo-state.js:96-113 + hooks/stilo-instructions.js:343-349: the one-level-down scan and buildAmbiguityNote list every matching child path with no count limit, and buildInjectedContext returns the full, unbudgeted context for status 'ambiguous' (:318), so a directory with thousands of <child>/.stilo/state.json entries produces an arbitrarily large SessionStart/SubagentStart injection; cap the listed entries (e.g. first 10 plus a count).

hooks/stilo-prompt.js:6-13 resolves the project from host-supplied data.cwd while hooks/stilo-activate.js:9 and hooks/stilo-subagent.js:8 use process.cwd(); if the host's cwd and the hook process cwd ever differ, the per-prompt state line and the session/subagent context can describe different projects. Use one source consistently.

hooks/stilo-state.js:87,132 use existsSync/readFileSync, which follow a symlinked/junctioned .stilo or state.json; content of the link target is only surfaced as a validated/truncated diagnostic (e.g. invalid phase up to 120 chars) to the same user's agent, so no cross-principal disclosure, but an lstat check would keep discovery inside the project tree.
